theory.title: Suite Setup and Teardown for Test Initialization
theory.content:
## Suite-Level Test Lifecycle

Robot Framework provides **suite-level** setup and teardown mechanisms that run **once per test file**, not once per test case. This enables efficient initialization of expensive resources that can be shared across multiple tests.

### Suite Setup

**Suite Setup** executes a single keyword **before any test cases** in the suite run:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Log    Starting Test Suite

*** Test Cases ***
Test One
    Log    First test

Test Two
    Log    Second test
```

**Execution order:**
1. Suite Setup: `Log Starting Test Suite`
2. Test One executes
3. Test Two executes

### When to Use Suite Setup

Common scenarios:

**Database initialization:**
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    DatabaseLibrary
Suite Setup    Connect To Database    mydb    user    pass    host    port
Suite Teardown    Disconnect From Database
```

**Browser initialization (shared session):**
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary
Suite Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
Suite Teardown    Close All Browsers
```

**Test data creation:**
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Create Test Users
Suite Teardown    Delete Test Users
```

**API authentication:**
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Authenticate API Client
Suite Teardown    Revoke API Token
```

### Suite Setup vs. Test Setup

**Suite Setup:**
- Runs **once** before all tests
- Shared state across tests
- Use for expensive initialization
- Faster execution (one-time cost)

**Test Setup:**
- Runs **before each test**
- Fresh state per test
- Use for test isolation
- Slower but more reliable

**Example comparison:**

```robot
# Suite Setup: Browser opened once, shared by all tests
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
Suite Teardown    Close Browser

*** Test Cases ***
Test Navigation
    Click Link    About
    Page Should Contain    About Us

Test Search
    Input Text    id:search    robot
    # Uses same browser from Suite Setup
```

```robot
# Test Setup: Fresh browser for each test
*** Settings ***
Test Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
Test Teardown    Close Browser

*** Test Cases ***
Test Navigation
    Click Link    About
    Page Should Contain    About Us
    # Browser closes after

Test Search
    # New browser opens
    Input Text    id:search    robot
```

### Suite Setup Syntax

```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Keyword Name
Suite Setup    Keyword With Args    arg1    arg2
Suite Setup    ${VARIABLE_HOLDING_KEYWORD}
```

**Multiple operations:**

Since Suite Setup accepts only **one keyword**, use compound keywords:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Initialize Test Environment

*** Keywords ***
Initialize Test Environment
    Log    Starting suite
    Connect To Database    mydb
    Load Test Data
    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
```

Or use `Run Keywords`:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Run Keywords
...    Log    Starting suite    AND
...    Connect To Database    mydb    AND
...    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
```

### Benefits of Suite Setup

**1. Performance:**
```robot
# Without Suite Setup: Open browser 100 times (slow)
Test Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
Test Teardown    Close Browser

# With Suite Setup: Open browser once (fast)
Suite Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
Suite Teardown    Close Browser
```

**2. Resource efficiency:**
- One database connection instead of N
- One authentication token instead of N
- One initialization instead of N

**3. Realistic scenarios:**
- Tests mimic real user sessions (multiple actions in one session)
- Simulates continuous application usage

### Risks and Considerations

**State pollution:**
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Login As Admin
Suite Teardown    Logout

*** Test Cases ***
Test 1
    Create User    newuser
    # User now exists in system

Test 2
    # Test 2 sees user created by Test 1!
    # May cause unexpected failures
```

**Solution:** Clean state between tests:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Login As Admin
Test Teardown    Delete All Test Data
Suite Teardown    Logout
```

**Failure impact:**

If Suite Setup **fails**, all tests in the suite are **skipped**:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Connect To Database    invalid_credentials

*** Test Cases ***
Test 1
    # SKIPPED - Suite Setup failed

Test 2
    # SKIPPED - Suite Setup failed
```

**Best practice:** Make Suite Setup robust:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Initialize With Retry

*** Keywords ***
Initialize With Retry
    Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    3x    5s    Connect To Database    ...
```

### Suite Teardown

**Suite Teardown** executes **after all tests** complete, even if tests fail:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup    Open Browser    ${URL}    Chrome
Suite Teardown    Close All Browsers

*** Test Cases ***
Test That Fails
    Fail    This test fails

Test That Passes
    Log    This test passes

# Suite Teardown STILL runs: Close All Browsers
```

**Common uses:**
- Close connections
- Delete temporary files
- Archive logs
- Send notifications
- Cleanup test data

### Complete Example

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library           SeleniumLibrary
Library           DatabaseLibrary
Suite Setup       Initialize Test Suite
Suite Teardown    Cleanup Test Suite
Test Setup        Reset Application State

*** Variables ***
${URL}            https://example.com
${DB_NAME}        testdb

*** Test Cases ***
Test User Registration
    Go To Registration Page
    Fill Registration Form    user1@example.com
    Submit Form
    User Should Be In Database    user1@example.com

Test User Login
    Login As User    user1@example.com    password
    Dashboard Should Be Visible

*** Keywords ***
Initialize Test Suite
    Log    Starting Test Suite    console=yes
    Connect To Database    ${DB_NAME}    user    pass    localhost    3306
    Open Browser    ${URL}    headlesschrome
    Maximize Browser Window

Cleanup Test Suite
    Close All Browsers
    Execute SQL String    DELETE FROM users WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com'
    Disconnect From Database
    Log    Test Suite Complete    console=yes

Reset Application State
    Go To    ${URL}
    Delete All Cookies
```

### Best Practices

1. **Keep Suite Setup fast:** Under 5 seconds ideal
2. **Make it idempotent:** Safe to run multiple times
3. **Handle failures gracefully:** Use retries and error handling
4. **Clean up in teardown:** Always release resources
5. **Document dependencies:** Explain what setup requires
6. **Test isolation:** Prevent tests from affecting each other

By mastering Suite Setup and Teardown, you create **efficient, maintainable test suites** that initialize once and run quickly.
learningObjectives: Understand the difference between Suite Setup and Test Setup
Use Suite Setup to perform one-time initialization before all tests
Recognize when to use suite-level vs. test-level setup
Implement efficient resource sharing across multiple tests

exercises.title: Test Templates
exercises.description: Use test templates for data-driven testing.
instructions: Create test 'Addition Tests' with [Template] Verify Addition
exercises.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
# Add templated test

*** Keywords ***
# Add verification keyword
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Addition Tests
    [Template]    Verify Addition
    1    1    2
    2    3    5
    5    5    10

*** Keywords ***
Verify Addition
    [Arguments]    ${a}    ${b}    ${expected}
    ${result}    Evaluate    ${a} + ${b}
    Should Be Equal    ${result}    ${expected}
hints: [Template] makes each data row a test
Each row passes arguments to the keyword
No keyword names needed in test rows
Great for testing multiple data sets
